aliases: information about one variable from another
purpose: Split book uncertainty into the part shared with the lamp and the part left after observing it.
meaning: Mutual information measures dependence between two random variables. For finite variables, I(X;Y)=H(X)−H(X|Y). It is symmetric and nonnegative, and vanishes exactly when the variables are independent. A consistently inverted observation can retain full information.

definition.setting: An assumed binary library return-tray model: X records book presence and Y records the sensor lamp.
definition.formal_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)=H(X)+H(Y)-H(X,Y)\geq0,\quad I(X;Y)=0\iff X\perp Y.

signature.Y: Binary sensor-lamp random variable: 0 off, 1 on.

signature.e: Symmetric channel flip probability, the same for each input state.
signature.yₛ: Selected observed lamp value, either 0 or 1.

signature.p₀₁: Joint probability of an empty tray and lamp on.
signature.p₁₀: Joint probability of a book and lamp off.

signature.p_Y(y): Marginal probability P(Y=y), after summing over X.
signature.P(X=x|Y=y): Conditional probability in a positive-probability lamp column.
signature.I(X;Y): Mutual information between book presence and the lamp, measured in bits.

signature.H(X|Y): Averaged remaining book uncertainty after observing the lamp.

conditions: X records presence in one library return tray: 0 means empty and 1 means a book. Y records its sensor lamp: 0 means off and 1 means on. This binary presence model differs from the preceding lesson’s three possible book counts. The channel probabilities are assumed for teaching, not fitted sensor measurements.

The prior book probability q=P(X=1) and symmetric flip probability e lie in [0,1]. The same channel rule gives P(Y≠X|X=x)=e for each possible input value x; a row with zero prior mass still has a specified channel rule.
The joint masses are p₀₀=(1−q)(1−e), p₀₁=(1−q)e, p₁₀=qe and p₁₁=q(1−e). The first index belongs to X and the second to Y. All four masses are nonnegative and add to one.
Marginal distributions come from summing rows or columns. A conditional distribution given Y=y is formed only when P(Y=y)>0; then divide the selected column by its total.
The selected lamp value yₛ is a view selection. Changing it does not alter the joint distribution or any averaged entropy or mutual information.

All logarithms in these finite information quantities use base two and the unit is bits. Terms with zero joint or marginal mass are omitted from their entropy sums using the continuous zero-term convention.
H(X|Y) is the probability-weighted average of the defined slice entropies H(X|Y=y). A zero-probability column has no defined conditional distribution, and is omitted from this weighted average.
Mutual information is I(X;Y)=H(X)−H(X|Y)=H(Y)−H(Y|X). It is symmetric, nonnegative and at most min(H(X),H(Y)); it describes dependence, without establishing a causal direction.
definition.domain_notes: Mutual information summarizes the whole joint distribution, not the one selected lamp reading. It is distinct from outcome surprisal I(x). This finite dependence measure establishes no causal direction.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original finite calculations; independent review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)=H(X)+H(Y)-H(X,Y)\geq0,\quad I(X;Y)=0\iff X\perp Y.
grammar.formation_rule: First use q and 1−q for the book-presence probabilities. Split each row with channel probabilities 1−e and e, keeping the X index first and Y index second. Sum the joint masses across the other variable to get a marginal distribution. Divide a selected lamp column by its positive marginal total to obtain the conditional distribution. Compute prior entropy and averaged conditional entropy from that same joint distribution. Their difference is mutual information. The entropy chain rule gives the equivalent symmetric expression H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y). A deterministic inverted observation can be decoded exactly.
grammar.precedence: Multiply the prior by a channel probability to form a joint cell. Add cells to form marginals. Normalize only positive-probability conditioning columns, then apply base-two entropy formulas.

properties.claim: Mutual information is symmetric, nonnegative and bounded by both marginal entropies.
properties.conditions: Use finite random variables and their single common joint distribution.
properties.derivation: The entropy identities and nonnegativity of conditional entropy give I(X;Y)=I(Y;X) and 0≤I(X;Y)≤min(H(X),H(Y)).
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent mathematical review pending

properties.claim: A one-to-one relabeling preserves full information.
properties.conditions: The inverse observation rule is known and deterministic on the support.
properties.derivation: At e=1, X=1−Y; each observed lamp value fixes X, so H(X|Y)=0 and I(X;Y)=H(X).
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent mathematical review pending

prompts.prompt: Can a perfectly inverted lamp carry all information about a book?
prompts.answer: Yes. If the inverse label rule is known, Y determines X exactly and no conditional uncertainty remains.

prompts.prompt: Does symmetric mutual information identify which variable causes the other?
prompts.answer: No. Mutual information is a dependence measure and provides no causal direction on its own.
